1985.notes: Arizona Department of Revenue 1986 Annual Report (fiscal year 1985-86; Internet Archive state-documents microfiche), 'Individual income tax - major features' (PDF page index 49): 'Individual rates are graduated from a minimum of 2% on individual income of $1,123, or joint income of $2,246, to a maximum of 8% on individual income over $6,738, or joint income over $13,476. Individual tax brackets are annually indexed for inflation.' The report describes tax year 1985 (the DOR's 1983-84 report gives the 1983 amounts and the 1987 and 1988 reports the 1986 and 1987 amounts; the same page refers to credits 'for the 1985 tax year'). The report prints only the first and top brackets (and their joint doubles); the intermediate bracket starts are written as 2x-5x the printed first bracket, because Laws 1982, ch. 75 indexes every bracket's limits by the same CPI factor and every printed year (1983, 1984, 1986, 1988) shows exact multiples. Deduction = personal exemption $1,941 single / $3,882 married and standard deduction 19.4% of income, max $971 / $1,941, from the report's Table 29 'Exemptions, deductions & credits indexed to inflation', tax year 1985 row (page n55; the 1987 and 1988 reports print the same row). Federal income tax paid is deductible from income (not modelled). Community property state (in general half the community income is taxable to each spouse).

1986.notes: Arizona Department of Revenue 1987 Annual Report (fiscal year 1986-87; Internet Archive state-documents microfiche), 'Individual income tax - major features' (PDF page index 50): 'Individual rates are graduated from a minimum of 2% on individual income of $1,155, or joint income of $2,310, to a maximum of 8% on individual income over $6,930, or joint income over $13,860' (tax year 1986; the same page refers to credits 'for the 1986 tax year'). The full 1986 schedule as written here is the one printed in ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1987 ed., Table 51 (rates for tax year 1986; bracket amounts exactly double for married filing jointly). Deduction = personal exemption $1,996 single / $3,992 married and standard deduction 19.96% of income, max $998 / $1,996, from the report's Table 29 'Exemptions, deductions & credits indexed to inflation', tax year 1986 row (page n56; the 1988 report prints the same row). The ACIR 1987 ed. Table 50 printed $1,941 and 18.3% / $917 / $1,834 for 1986, which are the DOR's 1985 exemption and 1984 standard-deduction figures, so the DOR table is used. Federal income tax paid is deductible from income (not modelled). Community property state (in general half the community income is taxable to each spouse).

1987.notes: Arizona Department of Revenue 1988 Annual Report (fiscal year 1987-88; Internet Archive state-documents microfiche), 'Individual income tax - major features' (PDF page index 29): 'Rates are graduated from a minimum of 2% on individual income of $1,183 (or joint income of $2,366) to a maximum of 8% on individual income over $7,098 (or joint income over $14,196). Individual tax brackets are indexed annually for inflation.' The report describes tax year 1987 (its Table 29 runs through tax year 1987; the 1986 and 1987 reports give the 1985 and 1986 amounts). The report prints only the first and top brackets (and their joint doubles); the intermediate bracket starts are written as 2x-5x the printed first bracket, because Laws 1982, ch. 75 indexes every bracket's limits by the same CPI factor and every printed year (1983, 1984, 1986, 1988) shows exact multiples. Deduction = personal exemption $2,045 single / $4,090 married and standard deduction 20.45% of income, max $1,023 / $2,045, from Table 29 'Exemptions, deductions & credits indexed to inflation', tax year 1987 row (page n67). Federal income tax paid is deductible from income (not modelled). For 1987 only, Laws 1987, 2nd S.S., ch. 2 let taxpayers subtract the greater of 46% of their 1987 federal income tax liability or $475 (not modelled). Community property state (in general half the community income is taxable to each spouse).
